ER → Relational mapping algorithm (steps from slides)

 STEPS 1–7 (ER) AND 8–9 (EER)
 1. Regular entity → table with all simple attributes (composite → its simple parts); pick a primary key.
 2. Weak entity → table with its attributes + owner's PK as foreign key; PK = (owner PK + partial key).
 3. Binary 1:1 → (a) foreign key in the side with total participation, or (b) merge both into one table, or (c) separate
 relationship table.
 4. Binary 1:N → put PK of the “1” side as a foreign key in the “N” side table (+ relationship attributes).
 5. Binary M:N → new table with both PKs as foreign keys; PK = their combination; add relationship attributes.
 6. Multivalued attribute → new table (attribute + owner PK); PK = combination.
 7. N-ary (n>2) → new table with n foreign keys (PK = combination, e.g. SUPPLY(SName, PartNo, ProjName)).
 8. Specialization/generalization → options 8A–8D (see 1.2). 9. Union type (category) → new table with a surrogate
 key.

 1.3 EER Case-Study Design (“Draw the EER diagram”) 🔴 Must-do
 METHOD TO SOLVE ANY EER SCENARIO (USE FOR EVERY CASE STUDY)
 1. Underline all nouns → candidate entities; verbs → relationships; adjectives/values → attributes.
 2. Identify the common attributes → super-class (generalization); special attributes → sub-classes.

 2.2 Normalization (1NF → 5NF) 🟡 Important Not in slides


 DEFINITION
 Normalization is the process of organising relations using functional (FD), multivalued (MVD) and join dependencies so
 that redundancy and update anomalies (insertion, deletion, modification) are removed, by decomposing into smaller
 relations that are lossless and, ideally, dependency-preserving.


Rules & formulas
 FD X→Y: two tuples equal on X must be equal on Y. Armstrong: reflexivity (Y⊆X ⇒ X→Y), augmentation (X→Y ⇒ XZ→YZ),
 transitivity (X→Y, Y→Z ⇒ X→Z). Derived: union, decomposition, pseudo-transitivity.
 Closure X⁺ = all attributes functionally determined by X. Algorithm: start X⁺=X; repeat: if some FD A→B has A⊆X⁺, add B;
 stop when no change. Candidate key = minimal X with X⁺ = all attributes. Attributes never on any RHS must be in every
 key.




ADBMS Exam Notes Made by Jay Naik Page 25 of 100

NF Condition Removes

 1NF all attribute values atomic; no repeating groups multi-valued cells

 2NF 1NF + no partial dependency (non-prime attr depends on part of a candidate key) partial dependencies

 3NF 2NF + no transitive dependency; for every X→A: X superkey or A prime transitive dependencies

 BCNF for every non-trivial X→A, X is a superkey anomalies from overlapping
 keys

 4NF BCNF + no non-trivial multivalued dependency X→→Y unless X is a superkey independent multi-valued
 facts

 5NF 4NF + every join dependency is implied by candidate keys (cannot be losslessly join dependencies
 (PJNF) decomposed further)


 WORKED NUMERICAL: R(A,B,C,D,E), F = {AB→C, B→D, C→E}
 Step 1 – Candidate key. RHS attributes: C, D, E. Attributes never on RHS: A, B ⇒ key must contain A and B. Compute
 (AB)⁺: start {A,B}; AB→C ⇒ {A,B,C}; B→D ⇒ {A,B,C,D}; C→E ⇒ {A,B,C,D,E} = all. So AB is the only candidate key; prime =
 {A,B}.
 Step 2 – 1NF holds (atomic).
 Step 3 – 2NF test. B→D: D is non-prime and depends on part (B) of key AB ⇒ partial dependency, not in 2NF.
 Decompose: R1(B,D) [F: B→D], R2(A,B,C,E) [F: AB→C, C→E]. Lossless because B (common) is a key of R1.
 Step 4 – 3NF test on R2. Key AB. C→E: C not a superkey, E non-prime ⇒ transitive (AB→C→E) ⇒ not 3NF. Decompose
 R2: R21(C,E), R22(A,B,C).
 Step 5 – Final: R1(B,D), R21(C,E), R22(A,B,C). Each determinant (B, C, AB) is a key of its own relation ⇒ BCNF; every
 original FD is preserved (B→D in R1, C→E in R21, AB→C in R22) ⇒ lossless and dependency-preserving.

 Supplies(Supplier, Part, Project) with the cyclic business rule “if S supplies P, J uses P and S supplies to J, then S supplies
 P to J”. Table (4 rows): (S1,P1,J1), (S1,P1,J2), (S1,P2,J1), (S2,P1,J1). It has no FD/MVD violation, but it equals the join of
 its three projections SP(Supplier,Part) = {(S1,P1),(S1,P2),(S2,P1)}, PJ(Part,Project) = {(P1,J1),(P1,J2),(P2,J1)} and
 SJ(Supplier,Project) = {(S1,J1),(S1,J2),(S2,J1)}. Check: joining the three gives exactly those 4 rows (e.g. (S1,P2,J2) is

 relations; the 3-way join reconstructs exactly the original (join dependency ⋈(SP, PJ, SJ)). 5NF is rare in practice;

CAP theorem and BASE
CAP: a distributed data store can guarantee only two of Consistency (every read sees the latest write), Availability (every

NoSQL counterpart of ACID.
